Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 76, verses 1–3:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah mentions in this surah the beginning state of man, his end, and his middle state. He mentions that there passed over him a long period of time (dahr), which was before his existence, when he was non-existent, indeed not even mentioned.

{2} Then, when He willed to create him, He created his father Adam from clay, and then made his offspring come into being in succession {from a drop of mingled fluid}; that is, water, humble and filthy. {We test him}: by this, so that We may know whether he will recall his former state and take heed of it, or whether he will forget it and be deceived by his own self. So Allah brought him into existence and created for him the outward and inward faculties, such as hearing, sight and the rest of the limbs, and He perfected them for him and made them sound, so that by them he is able to attain his aims.

{3} Then He sent to him the messengers, sent down to him the scriptures, guided him to the path that leads to Him, made it clear, encouraged him toward it, and informed him of what awaits him upon reaching Him. Then He informed him of the path that leads to destruction, warned him against it, informed him of what awaits him if he takes it, and tested him with that. Thus people became divided: some are thankful for Allah's blessing upon them, standing by the rights which Allah has laid upon them; and others are ungrateful for the blessings which Allah bestowed upon them, both religious and worldly, rejecting them, disbelieving in their Lord, and taking the path that leads to destruction. [Then He, exalted is He, mentions the two groups at the time of recompense, saying]:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 76, verses 1–3:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah mentions in this surah the beginning state of man, his end, and his middle state. He mentions that there passed over him a long period of time (dahr), which was before his existence, when he was non-existent, indeed not even mentioned.

{2} Then, when He willed to create him, He created his father Adam from clay, and then made his offspring come into being in succession {from a drop of mingled fluid}; that is, water, humble and filthy. {We test him}: by this, so that We may know whether he will recall his former state and take heed of it, or whether he will forget it and be deceived by his own self. So Allah brought him into existence and created for him the outward and inward faculties, such as hearing, sight and the rest of the limbs, and He perfected them for him and made them sound, so that by them he is able to attain his aims.

{3} Then He sent to him the messengers, sent down to him the scriptures, guided him to the path that leads to Him, made it clear, encouraged him toward it, and informed him of what awaits him upon reaching Him. Then He informed him of the path that leads to destruction, warned him against it, informed him of what awaits him if he takes it, and tested him with that. Thus people became divided: some are thankful for Allah's blessing upon them, standing by the rights which Allah has laid upon them; and others are ungrateful for the blessings which Allah bestowed upon them, both religious and worldly, rejecting them, disbelieving in their Lord, and taking the path that leads to destruction. [Then He, exalted is He, mentions the two groups at the time of recompense, saying]:

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. This perpetual punishment is everlasting for them: they abide in it forever and ever.

{5} As for {the righteous} (al-abrar), those whose hearts are upright (barrat qulubuhum) through what they contain of the knowledge of God, love for Him, and beautiful character, and whose deeds are likewise upright, as they employ themselves in deeds of righteousness, He informs us that they {drink from a cup}, that is, a delicious drink of wine [that has been] mixed with camphor, meaning it is blended with it to cool it and break its sharpness. This camphor is of the utmost delight, free of every turbidity and disturbance found in the camphor of this world, for the defects present in this world are absent from it. The names God mentioned for Paradise are of the same kind, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among lote-trees without thorns, and acacias arranged in tiers﴾, ﴿and pure spouses﴾, ﴿for them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴾, and ﴿therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in﴾.

{6} ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink﴾; that is, that delicious cup they drink from does not fear running out, for it has an inexhaustible source: a spring always gushing and flowing, which the servants of God cause to burst forth in abundance wherever they wish and however they desire. If they wish, they direct it to flourishing gardens, or to resplendent meadows, or among the sides of ornamented palaces and dwellings, or to whatever direction they see that is pleasing.

{7} Then He mentioned some of their deeds, saying: ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾; that is, they fulfil what they bound themselves to God with of vows and pledges. If they fulfil a vow, which is not obligatory upon them originally but only through their own obligating it upon themselves, then their performance and observance of the original obligations is all the more fitting and worthy. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾; that is, pervasive and spreading. They fear that its evil may reach them, so they abandon every cause that would bring it about.

{8–10} ﴿And they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾; that is, while they are in a state in which they love wealth and food, yet they give precedence to the love of God over the love of their own souls. In feeding, they seek out those most deserving and most in need: ﴿the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾. They intend by their spending and feeding the Face of God, may He be exalted, and they say with the tongue of their state: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾; that is, neither material recompense nor verbal praise. ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, extremely stern and evil, ﴿and difficult﴾, that is, constricted and narrow.

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. Thus He combined for them the bounties of the outward and the inward.

{12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. Perhaps God singled out silk because it is the outward clothing that indicates the state of its wearer.

{13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. The couches (al-arai'k) are thrones upon which are adorned garments. ﴿They see therein no sun﴾, that is, in Paradise, whose heat would harm them, ﴿nor frigid cold (zamharir)﴾, that is, severe cold. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. This is among the most wondrous of things: that dense silver, by the purity of its essence and the goodness of its ore, should be as clear as crystal. ﴿They have measured it with a measure﴾; that is, they measured the aforementioned vessels according to the measure of their quenching: not more and not less, for if it were more, its delight would diminish, and if less, it would not suffice for their quenching. It is also possible that the meaning is: the people of Paradise measured it by an amount that accords with their delight, so it came to them as they had measured it in their thoughts.

{17–18} ﴿And they will be given to drink therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿a cup﴾, which is the vessel full of wine and pure wine. ﴿Its mixture is ginger﴾, that is, it is blended with it to make its taste and fragrance pleasant. ﴿A spring therein﴾ [that is, in Paradise], ﴿called Salsabil﴾: it was named so for its smoothness, its delight, and its beauty.

{19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. He has spouses of the utmost beauty and goodness, combining the beauty of outward and inward, good and beautiful, enough to fill the heart with joy, delight and happiness. Around him are the eternal young boys and the everlasting servants, by whom comfort and tranquillity are attained, the pleasure of life is complete, and felicity is perfected. Above all this, and greatest of it, is attaining the pleasure of the Merciful Lord, hearing His address, the delight of His nearness, rejoicing in His good pleasure, and eternal abiding, with the bliss they are in increasing at every moment and every time. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. This is a promise God made to them, and God's promise is fulfilled, for none is more truthful in speech or in statement. And His words: ﴿and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾; that is, there is no turbidity in it in any way, purifying what is in their bellies of every harm and impurity.

{22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{23} His, may He be exalted, words after mentioning the bliss of Paradise: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down upon you the Qur'an in gradual revelation﴾. In it are the promise and the warning, and the explanation of all that the servants need. In it is the command to uphold His commands and laws in the most complete manner, to strive to implement them, and to be patient in that.

{24} Therefore He said: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾; that is, be patient with His decree (qadar) by not resenting it, and with His legislative judgment (din) by persisting in it, and let no obstacle hinder you from it. ﴿And do not obey﴾ among the obstinate who want to turn you away ﴿a sinner﴾, that is, one committing sin and disobedience, ﴿or a disbeliever﴾. For obedience to disbelievers, sinners and wrongdoers must be disobedience to God, for they command only what their souls desire.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. This absolute command has already been restricted by His words: ﴿O you wrapped in your garments! Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{27} His words: ﴿Indeed, these﴾, that is, those who deny you, O Messenger, after the signs have been made clear to them, and they have been encouraged and warned, yet this has not benefited them at all; rather they continue to prefer ﴿the immediate﴾ [world] and to be content with it, ﴿and leave behind them﴾, that is, before them, ﴿a heavy Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, whose length is fifty thousand years of what you count. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ It is as though they were created only for this world and for dwelling in it.

{28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. Therefore He who brought them into being in this state is able to restore them after their death for their recompense. He who transported them in this abode through these stages would not fitly leave them neglected, unordered, unforbidden, unrewarded and unpunished. Therefore He said: ﴿And if We wish, We can replace their likes with complete replacement﴾; that is, We can produce you for resurrection as another creation, and restore you as you are, with your very selves, while they are themselves like them.

{29} ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾, by which the believer is reminded and benefits from what it contains of warning and encouragement. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, that is, a path that leads to Him. God makes the truth and guidance clear, then gives people the choice between being guided by it or turning away from it, establishing the proof, so that whoever perishes perishes upon clear evidence and whoever lives lives upon clear evidence.

{30} ﴿And you do not will except that God wills﴾, for the will of God prevails. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: to Him belongs the wisdom in guiding the one who is guided and misguiding the one who is misguided.

{31} ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, favouring him with His care, granting him success in the causes of happiness, and guiding him to its paths. ﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, who chose misery over guidance, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, for their wrongdoing and transgression.

Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. {6} ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink﴾; that is, that delicious cup they drink from does not fear running out, for it has an inexhaustible source: a spring always gushing and flowing, which the servants of God cause to burst forth in abundance wherever they wish and however they desire. {11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{8–10} ﴿And they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾; that is, while they are in a state in which they love wealth and food, yet they give precedence to the love of God over the love of their own souls. They intend by their spending and feeding the Face of God, may He be exalted, and they say with the tongue of their state: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾; that is, neither material recompense nor verbal praise. ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, extremely stern and evil, ﴿and difficult﴾, that is, constricted and narrow.

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. Thus He combined for them the bounties of the outward and the inward.

{12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. Perhaps God singled out silk because it is the outward clothing that indicates the state of its wearer.

{13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. It is also possible that the meaning is: the people of Paradise measured it by an amount that accords with their delight, so it came to them as they had measured it in their thoughts.

{17–18} ﴿And they will be given to drink therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿a cup﴾, which is the vessel full of wine and pure wine. ﴿Its mixture is ginger﴾, that is, it is blended with it to make its taste and fragrance pleasant. ﴿A spring therein﴾ [that is, in Paradise], ﴿called Salsabil﴾: it was named so for its smoothness, its delight, and its beauty.

{19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{24} Therefore He said: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾; that is, be patient with His decree (qadar) by not resenting it, and with His legislative judgment (din) by persisting in it, and let no obstacle hinder you from it. ﴿And do not obey﴾ among the obstinate who want to turn you away ﴿a sinner﴾, that is, one committing sin and disobedience, ﴿or a disbeliever﴾. For obedience to disbelievers, sinners and wrongdoers must be disobedience to God, for they command only what their souls desire.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. This absolute command has already been restricted by His words: ﴿O you wrapped in your garments! Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{27} His words: ﴿Indeed, these﴾, that is, those who deny you, O Messenger, after the signs have been made clear to them, and they have been encouraged and warned, yet this has not benefited them at all; rather they continue to prefer ﴿the immediate﴾ [world] and to be content with it, ﴿and leave behind them﴾, that is, before them, ﴿a heavy Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, whose length is fifty thousand years of what you count. {28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. {26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. This perpetual punishment is everlasting for them: they abide in it forever and ever.

{5} As for {the righteous} (al-abrar), those whose hearts are upright (barrat qulubuhum) through what they contain of the knowledge of God, love for Him, and beautiful character, and whose deeds are likewise upright, as they employ themselves in deeds of righteousness, He informs us that they {drink from a cup}, that is, a delicious drink of wine [that has been] mixed with camphor, meaning it is blended with it to cool it and break its sharpness. {6} ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink﴾; that is, that delicious cup they drink from does not fear running out, for it has an inexhaustible source: a spring always gushing and flowing, which the servants of God cause to burst forth in abundance wherever they wish and however they desire. If they wish, they direct it to flourishing gardens, or to resplendent meadows, or among the sides of ornamented palaces and dwellings, or to whatever direction they see that is pleasing.

{7} Then He mentioned some of their deeds, saying: ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾; that is, they fulfil what they bound themselves to God with of vows and pledges. {11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. {31} ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, favouring him with His care, granting him success in the causes of happiness, and guiding him to its paths. ﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, who chose misery over guidance, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, for their wrongdoing and transgression.

Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. This perpetual punishment is everlasting for them: they abide in it forever and ever.

{5} As for {the righteous} (al-abrar), those whose hearts are upright (barrat qulubuhum) through what they contain of the knowledge of God, love for Him, and beautiful character, and whose deeds are likewise upright, as they employ themselves in deeds of righteousness, He informs us that they {drink from a cup}, that is, a delicious drink of wine [that has been] mixed with camphor, meaning it is blended with it to cool it and break its sharpness. This camphor is of the utmost delight, free of every turbidity and disturbance found in the camphor of this world, for the defects present in this world are absent from it. The names God mentioned for Paradise are of the same kind, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among lote-trees without thorns, and acacias arranged in tiers﴾, ﴿and pure spouses﴾, ﴿for them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴾, and ﴿therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in﴾.

{6} ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink﴾; that is, that delicious cup they drink from does not fear running out, for it has an inexhaustible source: a spring always gushing and flowing, which the servants of God cause to burst forth in abundance wherever they wish and however they desire. If they wish, they direct it to flourishing gardens, or to resplendent meadows, or among the sides of ornamented palaces and dwellings, or to whatever direction they see that is pleasing.

{7} Then He mentioned some of their deeds, saying: ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾; that is, they fulfil what they bound themselves to God with of vows and pledges. If they fulfil a vow, which is not obligatory upon them originally but only through their own obligating it upon themselves, then their performance and observance of the original obligations is all the more fitting and worthy. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾; that is, pervasive and spreading. They fear that its evil may reach them, so they abandon every cause that would bring it about.

{8–10} ﴿And they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾; that is, while they are in a state in which they love wealth and food, yet they give precedence to the love of God over the love of their own souls. In feeding, they seek out those most deserving and most in need: ﴿the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾. They intend by their spending and feeding the Face of God, may He be exalted, and they say with the tongue of their state: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾; that is, neither material recompense nor verbal praise. ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, extremely stern and evil, ﴿and difficult﴾, that is, constricted and narrow.

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. Thus He combined for them the bounties of the outward and the inward.

{12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. Perhaps God singled out silk because it is the outward clothing that indicates the state of its wearer.

{13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. The couches (al-arai'k) are thrones upon which are adorned garments. ﴿They see therein no sun﴾, that is, in Paradise, whose heat would harm them, ﴿nor frigid cold (zamharir)﴾, that is, severe cold. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. This is among the most wondrous of things: that dense silver, by the purity of its essence and the goodness of its ore, should be as clear as crystal. ﴿They have measured it with a measure﴾; that is, they measured the aforementioned vessels according to the measure of their quenching: not more and not less, for if it were more, its delight would diminish, and if less, it would not suffice for their quenching. It is also possible that the meaning is: the people of Paradise measured it by an amount that accords with their delight, so it came to them as they had measured it in their thoughts.

{17–18} ﴿And they will be given to drink therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿a cup﴾, which is the vessel full of wine and pure wine. ﴿Its mixture is ginger﴾, that is, it is blended with it to make its taste and fragrance pleasant. ﴿A spring therein﴾ [that is, in Paradise], ﴿called Salsabil﴾: it was named so for its smoothness, its delight, and its beauty.

{19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. Around him are the eternal young boys and the everlasting servants, by whom comfort and tranquillity are attained, the pleasure of life is complete, and felicity is perfected. Above all this, and greatest of it, is attaining the pleasure of the Merciful Lord, hearing His address, the delight of His nearness, rejoicing in His good pleasure, and eternal abiding, with the bliss they are in increasing at every moment and every time. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. {12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. {13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. {19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. {21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. He has spouses of the utmost beauty and goodness, combining the beauty of outward and inward, good and beautiful, enough to fill the heart with joy, delight and happiness. Around him are the eternal young boys and the everlasting servants, by whom comfort and tranquillity are attained, the pleasure of life is complete, and felicity is perfected. Above all this, and greatest of it, is attaining the pleasure of the Merciful Lord, hearing His address, the delight of His nearness, rejoicing in His good pleasure, and eternal abiding, with the bliss they are in increasing at every moment and every time. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{23} His, may He be exalted, words after mentioning the bliss of Paradise: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down upon you the Qur'an in gradual revelation﴾. In it is the command to uphold His commands and laws in the most complete manner, to strive to implement them, and to be patient in that.

{24} Therefore He said: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾; that is, be patient with His decree (qadar) by not resenting it, and with His legislative judgment (din) by persisting in it, and let no obstacle hinder you from it. ﴿And do not obey﴾ among the obstinate who want to turn you away ﴿a sinner﴾, that is, one committing sin and disobedience, ﴿or a disbeliever﴾. For obedience to disbelievers, sinners and wrongdoers must be disobedience to God, for they command only what their souls desire.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. This absolute command has already been restricted by His words: ﴿O you wrapped in your garments! Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{27} His words: ﴿Indeed, these﴾, that is, those who deny you, O Messenger, after the signs have been made clear to them, and they have been encouraged and warned, yet this has not benefited them at all; rather they continue to prefer ﴿the immediate﴾ [world] and to be content with it, ﴿and leave behind them﴾, that is, before them, ﴿a heavy Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, whose length is fifty thousand years of what you count. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ It is as though they were created only for this world and for dwelling in it.

{28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. Therefore He who brought them into being in this state is able to restore them after their death for their recompense. He who transported them in this abode through these stages would not fitly leave them neglected, unordered, unforbidden, unrewarded and unpunished. Therefore He said: ﴿And if We wish, We can replace their likes with complete replacement﴾; that is, We can produce you for resurrection as another creation, and restore you as you are, with your very selves, while they are themselves like them.

{29} ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾, by which the believer is reminded and benefits from what it contains of warning and encouragement. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, that is, a path that leads to Him. God makes the truth and guidance clear, then gives people the choice between being guided by it or turning away from it, establishing the proof, so that whoever perishes perishes upon clear evidence and whoever lives lives upon clear evidence.

{30} ﴿And you do not will except that God wills﴾, for the will of God prevails. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: to Him belongs the wisdom in guiding the one who is guided and misguiding the one who is misguided.

{31} ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, favouring him with His care, granting him success in the causes of happiness, and guiding him to its paths. ﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, who chose misery over guidance, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, for their wrongdoing and transgression.

Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. {31} ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, favouring him with His care, granting him success in the causes of happiness, and guiding him to its paths. ﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, who chose misery over guidance, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, for their wrongdoing and transgression.

Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. This perpetual punishment is everlasting for them: they abide in it forever and ever.

{5} As for {the righteous} (al-abrar), those whose hearts are upright (barrat qulubuhum) through what they contain of the knowledge of God, love for Him, and beautiful character, and whose deeds are likewise upright, as they employ themselves in deeds of righteousness, He informs us that they {drink from a cup}, that is, a delicious drink of wine [that has been] mixed with camphor, meaning it is blended with it to cool it and break its sharpness. This camphor is of the utmost delight, free of every turbidity and disturbance found in the camphor of this world, for the defects present in this world are absent from it. The names God mentioned for Paradise are of the same kind, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among lote-trees without thorns, and acacias arranged in tiers﴾, ﴿and pure spouses﴾, ﴿for them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴾, and ﴿therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in﴾.

{6} ﴿A spring from which the servants of God drink﴾; that is, that delicious cup they drink from does not fear running out, for it has an inexhaustible source: a spring always gushing and flowing, which the servants of God cause to burst forth in abundance wherever they wish and however they desire. If they wish, they direct it to flourishing gardens, or to resplendent meadows, or among the sides of ornamented palaces and dwellings, or to whatever direction they see that is pleasing.

{7} Then He mentioned some of their deeds, saying: ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾; that is, they fulfil what they bound themselves to God with of vows and pledges. If they fulfil a vow, which is not obligatory upon them originally but only through their own obligating it upon themselves, then their performance and observance of the original obligations is all the more fitting and worthy. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾; that is, pervasive and spreading. They fear that its evil may reach them, so they abandon every cause that would bring it about.

{8–10} ﴿And they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾; that is, while they are in a state in which they love wealth and food, yet they give precedence to the love of God over the love of their own souls. In feeding, they seek out those most deserving and most in need: ﴿the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾. They intend by their spending and feeding the Face of God, may He be exalted, and they say with the tongue of their state: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you no reward nor thanks﴾; that is, neither material recompense nor verbal praise. ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, extremely stern and evil, ﴿and difficult﴾, that is, constricted and narrow.

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. Thus He combined for them the bounties of the outward and the inward.

{12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. Perhaps God singled out silk because it is the outward clothing that indicates the state of its wearer.

{13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. The couches (al-arai'k) are thrones upon which are adorned garments. ﴿They see therein no sun﴾, that is, in Paradise, whose heat would harm them, ﴿nor frigid cold (zamharir)﴾, that is, severe cold. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. This is among the most wondrous of things: that dense silver, by the purity of its essence and the goodness of its ore, should be as clear as crystal. ﴿They have measured it with a measure﴾; that is, they measured the aforementioned vessels according to the measure of their quenching: not more and not less, for if it were more, its delight would diminish, and if less, it would not suffice for their quenching. It is also possible that the meaning is: the people of Paradise measured it by an amount that accords with their delight, so it came to them as they had measured it in their thoughts.

{17–18} ﴿And they will be given to drink therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿a cup﴾, which is the vessel full of wine and pure wine. ﴿Its mixture is ginger﴾, that is, it is blended with it to make its taste and fragrance pleasant. ﴿A spring therein﴾ [that is, in Paradise], ﴿called Salsabil﴾: it was named so for its smoothness, its delight, and its beauty.

{19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. Around him are the eternal young boys and the everlasting servants, by whom comfort and tranquillity are attained, the pleasure of life is complete, and felicity is perfected. Above all this, and greatest of it, is attaining the pleasure of the Merciful Lord, hearing His address, the delight of His nearness, rejoicing in His good pleasure, and eternal abiding, with the bliss they are in increasing at every moment and every time. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{11} ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day﴾: the greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ ﴿And He gave them radiance﴾; that is, He honoured them and bestowed upon them {radiance} in their faces and {joy} in their hearts. {12} ﴿And He rewarded them for their patience﴾ in obeying Him, when they did what they could of it; in refraining from His disobedience, when they abandoned it; and in His painful decrees, when they did not resent them. {A garden} encompassing every bounty, safe from every turbidity and disturbance, ﴿and silk﴾, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. {13} ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Reclining (al-ittikaʼ) means being settled in sitting, in a state of tranquillity, ease and luxury. Rather, all their times are in a complete shade, with neither heat nor cold, so that the bodies enjoy it and are not pained by heat or cold.

{14} ﴿And its shades are near over them, and its fruit-clusters are made easy to reach, lowered in readiness﴾; that is, its fruits are brought near to the one who desires them, so that he attains them while standing, sitting, or reclining.

{15–16} ﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾, that is, the young boys and servants will go around among the people of Paradise, ﴿with vessels of silver and goblets, which were crystal, crystal of silver﴾; that is, their substance is silver, yet it has the clarity of crystal. {19} ﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ among the people of Paradise, in their food, drink and service, ﴿young boys made eternal﴾, that is, created from Paradise to remain; they do not change nor grow old, and they are of the utmost beauty. ﴿When you see them﴾ dispersed in their service, ﴿you would think them﴾, because of their beauty, ﴿scattered pearls﴾. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. {21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. This is part of the perfection of the delight of the people of Paradise: that their servants are the eternal young boys whose sight gladdens, who enter their dwellings secure from any reproach, and who bring them what they call for and what their souls desire.

{20} ﴿And when you look there﴾, that is, when you gaze upon what the people of Paradise are in of perfect bliss, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. Each one of them has palaces, dwellings and adorned, ornamented chambers beyond what description can encompass; and with him are flourishing gardens, near fruits, delicious produce, flowing rivers, pleasing meadows, and delightful, melodious birds, which seize hearts and gladden souls. He has spouses of the utmost beauty and goodness, combining the beauty of outward and inward, good and beautiful, enough to fill the heart with joy, delight and happiness. Around him are the eternal young boys and the everlasting servants, by whom comfort and tranquillity are attained, the pleasure of life is complete, and felicity is perfected. Above all this, and greatest of it, is attaining the pleasure of the Merciful Lord, hearing His address, the delight of His nearness, rejoicing in His good pleasure, and eternal abiding, with the bliss they are in increasing at every moment and every time. Glory be to the King, the Sovereign, the True, the Manifest, whose treasuries never run out and whose goodness never diminishes, just as His attributes have no end; there is no end to His righteousness and His bounty.

{21} ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade﴾; that is, garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), both green, which are the most noble kinds of silk: sundus is the thicker silk, and istabraq is the finer. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾; that is, bracelets of silver will be placed upon their hands, for men and women alike. {22} ﴿Indeed, this﴾ abundant recompense [and beautiful bounty] ﴿has been for you a reward﴾ for the deeds you put forward, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾; that is, God makes even a small part of it bring you a lasting bliss beyond counting.

{23} His, may He be exalted, words after mentioning the bliss of Paradise: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down upon you the Qur'an in gradual revelation﴾. In it is the command to uphold His commands and laws in the most complete manner, to strive to implement them, and to be patient in that.

{24} Therefore He said: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾; that is, be patient with His decree (qadar) by not resenting it, and with His legislative judgment (din) by persisting in it, and let no obstacle hinder you from it. ﴿And do not obey﴾ among the obstinate who want to turn you away ﴿a sinner﴾, that is, one committing sin and disobedience, ﴿or a disbeliever﴾. For obedience to disbelievers, sinners and wrongdoers must be disobedience to God, for they command only what their souls desire.

{25} Since patience is nourished by performing the obedience of God and frequently remembering Him, God commanded that, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾; that is, at the beginning and end of the day. This includes the obligatory prayers and what follows them of supererogatory prayers, remembrance, glorification, declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir) at these times.

{26} ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾; that is, increase your prostration to Him, which implies the abundance of prayer, ﴿and glorify Him through a long night﴾. This absolute command has already been restricted by His words: ﴿O you wrapped in your garments! Stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it...﴾

{27} His words: ﴿Indeed, these﴾, that is, those who deny you, O Messenger, after the signs have been made clear to them, and they have been encouraged and warned, yet this has not benefited them at all; rather they continue to prefer ﴿the immediate﴾ [world] and to be content with it, ﴿and leave behind them﴾, that is, before them, ﴿a heavy Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, whose length is fifty thousand years of what you count. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ It is as though they were created only for this world and for dwelling in it.

{28} Then He argued against them and for their resurrection with a rational proof, which is the proof from origination, saying: ﴿We created them﴾, that is, We brought them into existence from nothing, ﴿and strengthened their frames﴾, that is, We firmly established their creation with the sinews, veins, tendons, and outward and inward faculties, until the body was complete, perfected, and able to do whatever it wills. Therefore He who brought them into being in this state is able to restore them after their death for their recompense. He who transported them in this abode through these stages would not fitly leave them neglected, unordered, unforbidden, unrewarded and unpunished. Therefore He said: ﴿And if We wish, We can replace their likes with complete replacement﴾; that is, We can produce you for resurrection as another creation, and restore you as you are, with your very selves, while they are themselves like them.

{29} ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾, by which the believer is reminded and benefits from what it contains of warning and encouragement. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, that is, a path that leads to Him. God makes the truth and guidance clear, then gives people the choice between being guided by it or turning away from it, establishing the proof, so that whoever perishes perishes upon clear evidence and whoever lives lives upon clear evidence.

{30} ﴿And you do not will except that God wills﴾, for the will of God prevails. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: to Him belongs the wisdom in guiding the one who is guided and misguiding the one who is misguided.

{31} ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, favouring him with His care, granting him success in the causes of happiness, and guiding him to its paths. ﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, who chose misery over guidance, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, for their wrongdoing and transgression.

Completed. All praise is due to God.

{4} That is: We have prepared and readied for those who disbelieve in God, deny His messengers, and dare to disobey Him: {chains} in the Fire of Hell, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him﴾; {shackles} with which their hands are fettered to their necks and they are bound; and {a blazing fire}, that is, a fire that blazes within their bodies and burns their bodies, so that whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment.
